In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of vaccines against encapsulated microorganisms such as Cryptococcus neoforms, which is the most common cause of meningitis in AIDS patients.
developing vaccines for the treatment of cryptococcosis.
the identification and development of novel vaccines and immunotherapeutic agents for infectious diseases and cancer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

peptide mimotopes of polysaccharide antigens can induce a human antibody response in human antibody transgenic mice and can induce a protective antibody response to polysaccharide antigen in a mouse model of cryptococcosis.
the peptide mimotope of the Cryptococcal capsular polysacchride glucuronoxylomanan (GXM) was immunogenic, inducing anamnestic response to the GXM and was effective against Cryptococcal challenge.
peptide mimotopes are immunogenic and induce a human-like response in mice that express human immunoglobulins, including antibodies to the capsular polysacchride of Cryptococcus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that a peptide mimetic (P13) of the C. neoformanns polysaccharide (GXM) can be used to vaccinate mice against cryptococcal infection.
we have shown that a peptide mimotope of the Cryptococcal capsule can be used to generate antibodies to the capsule in a mouse that expresses human immunoglobulins.
the P13 peptide mimotopic epitope is a target for antibodies in human immunoglobulins.
